hook: SCP-3980 is a mystery file in which the anomaly is never described directly; everything comes secondhand from former staff whose memories don't agree. Go in expecting to assemble the picture from contradictions, and watch the background of the closing interview, which is short and quietly gruesome.
whyItMatters: In place of a description, the article offers a list of mutually exclusive claims, each tagged with the person who made it, so the reader has to treat testimony as evidence rather than fact. That turns a containment report into something close to a whodunit, complete with an execution waiting for whoever is found guilty. The tags (antimemetic, contagion, cadaver, mind-affecting) hint at the shape of the answer without spelling it out.
thingsToNotice: One line in the procedures is worth rereading after the interview: transmissions from the destroyed base are to be ignored because nobody survived, even though the detainees are described as staff who happened to be off-site. During Director Kim's 2014 interview the interviewer keeps swatting flies while the flesh around Kim's lips sloughs away, and when Kim finally says three words, the interviewer dies on the spot. He is then led, not carried, to the morgue, and four guards are needed to restrain him. The holding site's name is struck through and replaced, and a footnote reminds personnel that Site-5 does not exist.
